result.summary: Ensures all initial outbound connections (default 3) for private transaction broadcasts run to completion even if the transaction is received back from the network or becomes invalid in the mempool. Replaces immediate transaction removal upon receipt with a resolved status, preventing subsequent retry connections via TryGrantRetry while allowing scheduled initial sends to finish. Peer disconnections are tracked directly, and connection compensation in FinalizeNode checks whether the handshake succeeded rather than transaction receipt confirmation.
result.problem: When a privately broadcast transaction was received back from a peer before all initial connections were established, the node immediately removed the transaction and canceled any remaining unestablished connections. This introduced a timing side channel where adversaries returning a transaction quickly could suppress remaining outbound connections and correlate or deanonymize the broadcaster.
evidence: PR description: 'Intended as an alternative to #34707, addressing the theoretical timing attack described in https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/34707#issuecomment-5603256702. Also fixes theoretical timing attacks described in https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/29415#discussion_r2035693786.'
result.scope_notes: Alternative design to open PR #34707 for handling finished private broadcast transaction state.
result.card: Ensures all three initial outbound connections for private transaction broadcasts finish even if the transaction is received back from the network while connections are still pending. Previously, receiving the transaction back immediately canceled unstarted broadcast connections, introducing theoretical timing side channels that an adversary could exploit to detect or link private broadcasts. The change marks transactions resolved to prevent retries without truncating the initial batch, and replaces receipt tracking upon peer disconnect with handshake status. It serves as an alternative to PR 34707.

risk.why: A flaw in connection lifecycle management or private broadcast message handling could stall private broadcasts, leak originating node identities, or mismanage outbound peer connection limits.
